name: Optimized Source-Spectral Ratio
definition: For a union-closed orientation of a nonempty binary class and shared positive rooted ratios $q$, let $\alpha_C(q)$ be the minimum spectral radius over all nonempty closed positive source-row choices and let $\beta_C(q)$ be the maximum spectral radius over all full negative source-row choices. Put $d_{\mathrm{sp}}(C)=\inf_{q>0}\beta_C(q)/\alpha_C(q)$, with $\beta/\infty=0$, and define $\delta_{\mathrm{sp}}(C)$ as the minimum of $d_{\mathrm{sp}}$ over union-closed coordinate reflections; an empty minimum is $+\infty$.
normalization: Rows are divided by their positive-root coefficient before forming the matrices. A missing positive closed choice gives $\alpha=\infty$; an empty negative system gives $\beta=0$.
comments: Invariant under coordinate permutations and reflections. If a union-closed orientation exists, then $\delta_{\mathrm{sp}}(C)=\tau(C)^2$; without one the value is $+\infty$ and has no realizability interpretation. The optimizing coefficient infimum need not be attained.
